origins.section: An Atomic Update Retries Until Its compareAndSet Wins, So Its Function Can Run Many Times
LongAdder Counts Faster Under Contention Because No Single Variable Holds the Total
compute and merge Are Atomic for One Key, Not for an Action Across Keys
Values That Must Agree Need One Lock or One Immutable Holder Replaced by compareAndSet

recorded.prompt:q-points-audit:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-points-audit:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-points-audit:b: Refuted by 'otherwise it reads again and re-runs the function' and the 14,139,089 re-runs. Caveat: the JDK source the page shows keeps the computed value when the re-read value is unchanged (haveNext = (prev == (prev = get()))), i.e. a spurious weakCAS failure retries only the write. The prose does not mention this, so b is not wholly false per the page's own code, but under contention (value changed) the page settles it against b.
